title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing, fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Morgan Reyes
description: Context: Continuous batching has been the primary lever for reducing per-token cost, but under high tail load we observed request starvation, fairness inversions (large requests blocking many small low-latency requests), and inconsistent timeouts across backends. This PR tunes the continuous-batcher scheduler and related queueing primitives to improve fairness, add starvation prevention, and make timeout handling deterministic. Motivation: reduce 95/99 latency regressions during mixed workloads (short chat messages + long generation), eliminate classes of flaky e2e failures caused by inconsistent per-request timeouts, and provide better metrics for observed queueing behavior. Summary of changes: - Scheduler: introduce a hybrid queueing policy (weighted deficit round robin + age-prioritization) to balance throughput and per-request fairness. New config knobs: max_queue_age_ms, starving_threshold_ms, weight_class (small, medium, large). - Starvation prevention: track per-request enqueue time and promote older requests when they cross starving_threshold_ms; add a bounded promotion window to avoid oscillation. - Queueing improvements: split the waiting queue into priority lanes (latency-sensitive, default, background) with dynamic lane assignment based on token budget and model runtime estimates. - Timeouts: unify timeout handling by centralizing deadline propagation through SchedulerContext; ensure KV cache lookup and kernel invocation respect request deadlines to prevent wasted GPU work. - KV cache: add a soft prefetch hint from the scheduler for promoted requests to warm the KV cache where possible. - Metrics & tracing: add detailed queueing metrics (queue_time_histogram, queue_promotions_total, lane_assignments), tracer spans around promotion/dispatch, and an alerting SLO for queue_time > max_queue_age_ms. - Tests & benchmarks: new unit and integration tests for starvation scenarios, microbenchmarks showing 95% latency improvements for small requests under mixed load, and a canary config for gradual rollout. Rollout plan: feature-gate behind continuous-batcher.experiments.scheduler_v2 and staged rollout to Dedicated pools for one week, followed by hosted API Canary. If a regression is observed, automatic fallback to scheduler_v1 is supported via runtime config. Checklist: - [x] Scheduler implementation and unit tests - [x] Integration tests for starvation and fairness - [x] Benchmarks and perf analysis included - [x] Docs updated (continuous-batcher.md) - [x] Feature-flag + rollout plan - [x] Alerting dashboards updated Testing notes: - Local unit tests: pass. - CI integration tests: initially flaky on the promotion timer; fixed by replacing time.Sleep with a controllable clock in tests. - Benchmarks: synthetic mixed workload (70% small, 30% large) shows median small-request latency down 28% and p95 down 42% vs v1. Observability: New metrics require a Grafana dashboard patch (linked in comments) and an alert for queue_time_histogram p99 > max_queue_age_ms. Related: builds on prior batcher work (ENG-1601) and follows discussions in the scheduler design doc.

review_comments: Evan Liu: Can you explain how the promotion window avoids oscillation when there are bursts of mid-size requests? The PR text says bounded promotion but it's not obvious from the code.

Author (Morgan Reyes): The promotion window is implemented as a fixed upper bound (config: promotion_window_ms) and we only allow a request to be promoted once per window. That prevents ping-ponging. Added inline comment and unit test to demonstrate behavior.
Priya Nair: The deadline propagation change touches many callsites — did you verify that kernels won't run past deadlines on GPU? We had a regression in a previous change where work kept running.

Author: Yes — SchedulerContext now carries an absolute deadline and dispatch validates remaining_budget before kernel invocation. We added a guard in the CUDA kernel host loop to check deadline and cancel the call if exceeded; integration tests cover this.
Luca Romano: Benchmarks look promising. Can we add a canary rollout playbook to the PR notes so ops teams can safely enable?
Author: Added a rollout section in the description and an ops playbook link in the final comment; staging on Dedicated pools for 7 days and automated rollback on SLI breaches.
